content:
I've viewed 6 reference images. Let me analyze what I see:

**Test image observations:**
- Corn ear with husks pulled back
- Pinkish/salmon-colored inner husks
- Kernels mostly yellow but with some subtle discoloration/streaking
- No heavy concentrated mold at the tip or base
- Scattered minor kernel issues

**Initial prediction: Fusarium** - The pink/salmon husk coloration and scattered subtle kernel discoloration without heavy tip mold (which would indicate Gibberella) or base mold (Diplodia) point toward Fusarium ear rot.

Now let me check the attractor guide.

Fusarium is listed as over-predicted (6x wrong), with actual classes being Ear_rots_Aspergillus (3x), Ear_rots_Gibberella (2x), and Ear_rots_Diplodia (1x). I already viewed all three of these references. Let me reconsider:

- **Aspergillus**: olive-green powdery mold -- no green mold visible in the test image. Ruled out.
- **Gibberella**: pinkish-white mold concentrated at ear tip -- the test image has pinkish husks but no obvious concentrated mold at the tip. The Gibberella references showed much more severe pink-red mold.
- **Diplodia**: white mold from base, bleached husks -- test image doesn't show white mold growing from the base.

The test image shows: pinkish/salmon inner husks, kernels mostly intact with subtle scattered discoloration, no heavy concentrated mold at tip or base. This pattern -- scattered subtle kernel issues with pink/salmon coloration -- is most consistent with **Fusarium** (white to pink or salmon-colored mold on scattered kernels).

No concentrated mold at the tip (ruling out Gibberella) or base (ruling out Diplodia), and no green powdery mold (ruling out Aspergillus/Trichoderma). The scattered, mild nature with pink/salmon coloration matches Fusarium ear rot description."}
